title: Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (2014 Budget Measures No. 6) Bill 2014
short_title: Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (2014 Budget Measures No. 6) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change social security, student, family and seniors payments, including indexation, eligibility tests, overseas payment rules and support for community service providers.
It would rename the clean energy supplement and end its indexation from 20 September 2014, alongside temporary freezes of specified asset limits for income support.
Untaxed superannuation income would enter the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card assessment, with an exemption for existing cardholders' products purchased before 1 January 2015.
changes: The annual primary earner limit for Family Tax Benefit Part B would fall from $150,000 to $100,000.
The large family supplement would be limited to families with at least four children.
Disability Support Pension overseas payment would generally be limited to 28 days within 12 months.
Young Carer Bursary payments would be excluded from social security and veterans' income tests.
Relocation scholarships would stop for students moving within or between major cities.
A Western Australian pay equity decision would qualify for Commonwealth supplementation of affected community service providers.
summary.affected: Families, students, disability pensioners, seniors, young carers and affected community service providers are affected.

divisions.question: Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (2014 Budget Measures No. 6) Bill 2014 - Second Reading - Agree with the main idea of the bill

speeches.speaker: Bill Shorten
speeches.brief: Argued that Labor had blocked government cuts of up to $80 a week to pensions affecting 3.7 million pensioners, including protecting 700000 single-income families from losing family tax benefit B and stopping the pension eligibility age rising to 70, but criticised a deal with the Greens to scrap the seniors supplement worth $886.60 a year for singles.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Andrews
speeches.brief: Argued that the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (2014 Budget Measures No. 6) Bill 2014 would deliver $2.7 billion in budget savings through changes to supplements, indexation, portability periods, disability support assessments, student assistance, the Commonwealth seniors health card and family payments.
